label: thm:concrete-charact
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:concrete-charact}
  Let~$(\mathcal C, 
  \ifthenelse{\equal{-}{-}}{|{-}|}{|-|} 
  \def#1{\mathcal C} 
  \ifx#1\empty 
   
  \else 
  ^{\mathcal C} 
  \fi 
 
)$ be a concrete category. $\mathcal C$ is
  concretely equivalent to a presheaf category if and only if the following
  conditions are all satisfied:
  \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
  \item \label{thm:concrete-charact:iso} $ 
  \ifthenelse{\equal{-}{-}}{|{-}|}{|-|} 
  \def#1{\mathcal C} 
  \ifx#1\empty 
   
  \else 
  ^{\mathcal C} 
  \fi 
 
$ reflects isomorphisms,
  \item \label{thm:concrete-charact:colimits} $\mathcal C$ is cocomplete
    and~$ 
  \ifthenelse{\equal{-}{-}}{|{-}|}{|-|} 
  \def#1{\mathcal C} 
  \ifx#1\empty 
   
  \else 
  ^{\mathcal C} 
  \fi 
 
$ preserves all small colimits,
    
  \item \label{thm:concrete-charact:small} the collection of isomorphism
    classes of primitive elements of~$\operatorname{Elt}(\mathcal C)$ is small,
    
  \item \label{thm:concrete-charact:prim-exists} for every element~$(X,x) \in
    \operatorname{Elt}(C)$, there is a morphism~$(U,u) \rightarrow (X,x)$ for some primitive
    element~$(U,u)$,
    
  \item \label{thm:concrete-charact:prim-equal} given two morphisms~$f,g\colon
    (U,u) \rightarrow (X,x) \in \operatorname{Elt}(\mathcal C)$ where~$(U,u)$ is primitive, we have~$f =
    g$,
    
  \item \label{thm:concrete-charact:prim-iso} given two morphisms~$f\colon (U,u)
    \rightarrow (X,x)$ and~$g\colon (V,v) \rightarrow (X,x)$ of~$\operatorname{Elt}(\mathcal C)$ where both~$(U,u)$
    and~$(V,v)$ are primitive, there is an isomorphism~$\theta\colon (U,u) \rightarrow
    (V,v)$ such that~$g \circ \theta = f$. 
  \end{enumerate}

label: lem:polyplex-gen
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:polyplex-gen}
  Let $(U,u) \in \operatorname{Elt}(\mathbf{Pol}_{\omega}^*)$. Then, the following are equivalent:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),ref=(\roman*)]
  \item \label{lem:polyplex-gen:gen} $(U,u)$ is a polyplex and there exist
    $\alpha \in U$ such that $u = \alpha$,
  \item \label{lem:polyplex-gen:pushout} there exist polyplex
    liftings
    \[
      G^\epsilon \colon (U^\epsilon,u^\epsilon) \rightarrow (U,\partial^{\epsilon}(u))
    \]
    for $\epsilon \in \{-,+\}$, principal elements $(S,s)$ and $(T,t)$, and
    morphisms
    \begin{align*}
      F^{\epsilon-} \colon (S,s)&\rightarrow (U^\epsilon,\partial^-(u^\epsilon))
      &
      F^{\epsilon+} \colon (T,t)&\rightarrow (U^\epsilon,\partial^+(u^\epsilon))      
    \end{align*}
    for $\epsilon \in \{-,+\}$, such that, considering the pushout
    \[
      \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=20mm]
        S \sqcup T
        \ar[r,"{[F^{+-},F^{++}]}"]
        \ar[d,"{[F^{--},F^{-+}]}"']
        &
        U^+
        \ar[d,"\bar G^+",dotted]
        \\
        U^-
        \ar[r,"\bar G^-"',dotted]
        &
        \partial U
      \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    $(U,u)$ is isomorphic to $(\bar U,\bar \alpha)$, where $\bar U$ is
    obtained from $\partial U$ by adding a generator
    \[
      \bar \alpha : \bar G^-(u^-) \rightarrow \bar G^+(u^+)
      \makebox[0pt][l]{.}
    \]
  \end{enumerate}

body_md:
\label{prop:polyplex-lifting-unique}
  Given two morphisms~$L^1\colon (U^1,u_1) \rightarrow (\mathsf{P},u)$ and~$L^2\colon (U^2,u_2) \rightarrow (\mathsf{P},u)$
  of~$\operatorname{Elt}(\mathbf{Pol}_{\omega}^*)$ where both~$(U^1,u_1)$ and~$(U^2,u_2)$ are primitive, there is an
  isomorphism~$\Theta\colon (U^1,u_1) \rightarrow (U^2,u_2)$ such that~$L^2 \circ \Theta = L^1$.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:opol-concr-ps}
  The category $\mathbf{Pol}_{\omega}$ is a concrete presheaf category.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Following Makkai's proof of \cite[Theorem 4]{makkai2005word}, the base
  category of the presheaf category given by the above theorem is a small full
  subcategory of $\mathbf{Pol}_{\omega}$, whose objects are (the underlying polygraphs of)
  plexes, and such that every (underlying polygraph of a) plex is isomorphic to
  exactly one object of this subcategory. The objects of the latter can thus be
  easily enumerated, since they are in correspondence with the generators of the
  terminal polygraph~$\mathbf{1}$, as plex liftings.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
In~\cite{araujo2022computads}, \citeauthor{araujo2022computads} relies on
  \cite[Proposition 5.14]{dean2022computads}, which gives sufficient conditions
  for a category to be a presheaf category on a given full subcategory. The
  difference with \cite[Theorem~4]{makkai2005word} is that the latter is
  relative to a concrete presheaf structure, and is able to characterize the
  shape category as a full subcategory of primitive elements.

body_md:
The above generic factorization can be seen as a stronger version of
  \Cref{prop:conduche}. Indeed, given $k,l > 0$ and $i = \min(k,l) - 1$, there
  exists a polygraph $\mathsf{D}^{k,l}$ such that $ 
  \def-{-} 
  \def#1{(\mathsf{D}^{k,l})} 
  \def#2{(-)} 
  \def#3{(\mathsf{D}^{k,l})} 
  \ifx-#1
  #2
  \else
  #3
  \fi
^{* 
  \def#1{} 
  \ifx#1\empty 
   
  \else 
  , 
  \fi 
}$ is the free
  $\omega$\nobreakdash-pre\-ca\-te\-gory\xspace with one $k$\nobreakdash-cell\xspace $u_1$ and one $l$\nobreakdash-cell\xspace $u_2$, such that $\partial^+_i(u_1)
  = \partial^-_i(u_2)$. The construction of $\mathsf{D}^{k,l}$ can be seen to induce a
  polyplex $(\mathsf{D}^{k,l},u_1\mathbin{\ast}_i u_2)$ by \Cref{lem:polyplex-comp}. Writting $n$
  for $\max(k,l)$ and $F^{k,l} \colon D^n \rightarrow  
  \def-{-} 
  \def#1{(\mathsf{D}^{k,l})} 
  \def#2{(-)} 
  \def#3{(\mathsf{D}^{k,l})} 
  \ifx-#1
  #2
  \else
  #3
  \fi
^{* 
  \def#1{} 
  \ifx#1\empty 
   
  \else 
  , 
  \fi 
}$ for the functor
  sending the non-trivial $n$\nobreakdash-cell\xspace of $D^n$ to $u_1\mathbin{\ast}_i u_2$,
  \Cref{prop:conduche} amounts to observe that the $F^{k,l}$'s are generic by
  \Cref{prop:polyplex-generic}.

label: weak-division
title: Property
body_md:
\label{weak-division}
  Given an $\omega$\nobreakdash-pre\-ca\-te\-gory\xspace $C$ and an equivalence $u : x \rightarrow y \in C_1$, for any
  $1$\nobreakdash-cells\xspace $s,t : y \rightarrow z$ and for any $2$\nobreakdash-cell\xspace
  $w : u \mathbin{\ast}_0 s \Rightarrow u \mathbin{\ast}_0 t$,
  \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
  \item \label{wd-e} there is a $2$\nobreakdash-cell\xspace $v : s \Rightarrow t$ such that
    $u \mathbin{\ast}_0 v \sim w$,
    \[
      \begin{tikzcd}[row sep=1ex]
        &y\ar[dr,bend left,"s"]\\
        x\ar[ur,bend left,"u"]\ar[dr,bend right,"u"']\ar[rr,phantom,"w\Downarrow"]&&z\\
        &y\ar[ur,bend right,"t"']
      \end{tikzcd}
      \qquad\sim\qquad
      \begin{tikzcd}
        x\ar[r,"u"]&y\ar[r,bend left=50,"s"]\ar[r,bend right=50,"t"']\ar[r,phantom,"v\Downarrow"]&z
      \end{tikzcd}
    \]
  \item \label{wd-u} for any $2$\nobreakdash-cells\xspace $v,v':s\Rightarrow t$ such that
    $u\mathbin{\ast}_0v\sim w\sim u\mathbin{\ast}_0 v'$ we have $v\sim v'$.
  \end{enumerate}
head: environment
